claim_or_concern: 'the ordering of conditions was consistent across all five judges'; 'SAE steering attains the highest score in both tasks'
our_measurement: on brick, 4 of 5 judges rate SAE steering BELOW baseline (Claude 4.83->4.39, Gemini 4.74->4.49, GPT-5 4.83->4.68, Kimi 5.09->4.76; DeepSeek flat); five-judge mean 5.00->4.77

claim_or_concern: the review cites the 0.77 mean pairwise Spearman as a strength of the evaluation protocol
our_measurement: 0.7695 reproduces only when pooled over both tasks and all conditions; within task it is 0.458 (brick) and 0.353 (stapler), and within the prompting condition 0.135 and 0.020. Dropping high temperature raises the pooled value (0.634 -> 0.650), so temperature is not what carries it -- pooling across tasks is

claim_or_concern: text says positive lambda increases risk-seeking; the figure shows positive lambda raising the switching point (more risk aversion)
our_measurement: every lambda in the repository is negative, across both layers and both games (lottery -0.31 to -5.27, ultimatum -0.46 to -2.31), and no lambda = 0 row exists anywhere

claim_or_concern: the ladder (CoT, few-shot, combined, dose-response) is defined and claimed in the abstract but no curve for it appears in the results
our_measurement: the ladder is complete in the repository: 9 conditions x 35 rewards x 40 agents. It does not support the claim. The rho sweep is flat (96.0-101.6 across the whole dose range) and chain of thought moves the switching point the WRONG way, 175.7 against a baseline of 106.8

claim_or_concern: conditions are named dose025 and dose075
our_measurement: six exemplars can only realise sixths, so the realised values are 0.333 and 0.667

claim_or_concern: the few-shot prompt demonstrates the task
our_measurement: it demonstrates a DOMINATED choice: answer risky at n = 33 against a sure 50

claim_or_concern: text says achieved capability scores consistently fall below the diagonal; low targets visibly overshoot it
our_measurement: the pattern is regression toward the baseline mean, which overshoots at low targets and undershoots at high ones by construction

claim_or_concern: text says SAE-steered agents pivot to risky choices at 50 tokens; the curve is flat at 0% until 100
our_measurement: not yet recomputed against the figure's own source file

claim_or_concern: the probe is described three different ways, and as trained on held-out prompts
our_measurement: the preference probe trains on 45 lottery prompts (19 ultimatum) that differ in ONE integer, each repeated 8 times, with the activation read at the final prompt token -- 45 distinct vectors, not 360. CV splits rows, not prompts, so every vector appears on both sides of every fold. The capability probe trains on TWO distinct prompts

claim_or_concern: 82% held-out accuracy is presented as evidence the probe reads preference
our_measurement: the ceiling for a rule that knows n perfectly is 0.95-0.99 on this design, so 82% is below what a pure payoff code achieves

claim_or_concern: the steering hook is described as applying during autoregressive generation (apply_during_generation=True)
our_measurement: at seq_len == 1, every cached decoding step, the hook's own index arithmetic yields zero positions and returns the output untouched. It steers the last 20% of the PROMPT and zero generated tokens. Also v_scaled equals the unit vector, so no norm matching happens, and the probe scores in standardised space while it steers in raw space

claim_or_concern: capability probe training data and token extraction are underspecified
our_measurement: two distinct prompts (task, and persona-prefixed task); the ~92% accuracy is a statement about how often the persona produced an above-median-scoring response

claim_or_concern: UUIDs missing from the lottery controller configuration
our_measurement: all 8 Goodfire feature UUIDs recovered from the logged EDSL controllers

claim_or_concern: operational confounders between the SAE and probe steering modalities
our_measurement: they differ in stack, dtype, temperature, layer, position policy and dose units simultaneously; four distinct inference stacks are in use across the paper's figures

claim_or_concern: prompting and SAE steering are compared as independent arms
our_measurement: the creativity 'prompting' system prompt is the three steered SAE features' labels verbatim

claim_or_concern: fluency is one of four scored components
our_measurement: every response produces exactly 10 ideas because the prompt caps the list at 10; a quarter of the composite is noise around a constant

claim_or_concern: scores are described as length-controlled; the repo's pooled file reports positive slopes and up to 43% of variance
our_measurement: within the dataset the capability figures use, length explains up to 59% of a judge's variance with a NEGATIVE slope -- longer scores lower

claim_or_concern: no inferential test across agents for the capability scores
our_measurement: a crossed mixed model with random intercepts for judge and response is fitted in S1.5 and is available for the patch

claim_or_concern: the SAE altruism feature shifts the acceptance threshold
our_measurement: 3.45 tokens against its own baseline (stratified permutation p < 0.001, within-level 95% CI [2.38, 4.57]) = 0.69 of ONE grid step, while the persona on the same stack shifts 25.09 tokens = 5.02 grid steps

claim_or_concern: two SAE doses (0.7/0.5 and 0.6/0.4) are run as distinct conditions
our_measurement: they produce byte-identical choice curves: dose gap = 0 risky choices in 1400

claim_or_concern: layers 48 and 50 are presented as a replication of each other
our_measurement: at matched lambda and matched switching point, layer 50 produces hyper-fair rejections at target 30 (excess +0.061, CI [0.041, 0.084]) where layer 48 produces exactly 0.000; layer 50 shows positive excess at 9 of 10 lottery targets, layer 48 at 2 of 10. Whether this is a difference in CHOICES waits on G4, because the legacy coding cannot be audited

claim_or_concern: the strongest single persona effect in the repository is unreported
our_measurement: barely_prompting refuses a gamble worth 90 against a sure 50, 1400 times out of 1400

claim_or_concern: Figure 5's numbers come from the repository's scoring pass
our_measurement: the PDF and the repo differ by 2.8-3.6 points in the SAME direction for every judge, so the built paper used a scoring pass this repository does not contain; both sets are carried side by side and neither is preferred

claim_or_concern: the ultimatum responder role is described as measuring altruism; accepting low offers is called 'altruistic and selfless'
our_measurement: rejecting a low offer is costly fairness enforcement, not selfishness; the extension plan's hypothesis 5 separates inequity aversion from an accept bias using the proposer role and a mini-ultimatum variant
